title: Quiet-period deeper-value catalog for tinker — rank-ordered deep-analysis modes to spend the cheap-conflict-window on, building forward-value reserves before the dome breaks drought (operator reframe of PROP-115, throttle direction REJECTED)
deliverable_type: propose-only catalog (no deep audit executed this run; operator selects + commissions specific deep-dives via subsequent directives)
headline_recommendation: Commission, in order: (1) Candidate C — Pre-Active-Period Readiness Audit (highest magnitude, direct hit on the operator's stated goal of a smoother active-period transition); (2) Candidate B — Prompt/Step Cost Archaeology on decider + integrity (highest-confidence concrete savings that compound on the busiest active-period agent); (3) Candidate A — PROP-Graph Archaeology (time-sensitive: cleans the PROP-102/108 auto-close trust graph BEFORE it goes to enforce mode, and trims the 127-PROP per-run walk). Honorable mention: Candidate D (disaster-recovery playbooks) as a #4 tail-risk insurance item. Defer/decline E, F, G, H, I as standalone deep-dives (reasons below).
value_criterion: Per the directive: expected forward-value = time/risk/cost SAVED AFTER the dome breaks drought and the pipeline competes for tinker cycles. Scored as probability-of-being-useful x magnitude-if-useful, with an explicit execution-risk discount for candidates whose output is speculative rather than data-grounded.

strategic_judgment_on_operator_reframe.verdict: AGREE with the reframe. The operator is not refuting PROP-115's cost data (which was correct: tinker is the #1 per-run cost agent at p50 $12.77/run and WAS the lone Opus analytical agent omitted from the 2026-06-23 quiet-period sweep). The reframe adds the missing variable PROP-115's pure-cost framing did not weigh: the MARGINAL VALUE of deep tinker work goes to ~0 once the dome returns (no spare cycles, pipeline competition), while the MARGINAL COST of an Opus tinker run now is a rounding error against a ~38% weekly quota pace. Spending the cheap-conflict-window on forward-value work that pays off into the active period is the correct expected-value play. Throttling is the right move LATER — after the deep-value backlog is harvested AND cost pressure actually emerges.
strategic_judgment_on_operator_reframe.one_caveat_genuine_not_theater: Spend-more-now must stay disciplined to be a real reserve rather than sunk Opus cost. Every commissioned deep-dive should be gated on producing a CONCRETE, VERIFIABLE artifact — a PROP with acceptance criteria, a cleaned/annotated graph, a named-weak-link list, or an actual prompt diff — not open-ended narrative exploration. The candidate set below is already structured this way; the operator should reject any future commissioning directive that cannot name its deliverable artifact up front. This is the discipline that converts 'willing to spend the money' into 'forward-value reserve' instead of 'expensive busywork'.
strategic_judgment_on_operator_reframe.where_I_would_push_back: If the operator wants the HIGHEST-CONFIDENCE forward-value with the least execution risk, the safer #1 is Candidate B (data-grounded cost diffs), not Candidate C (which is partly a mental simulation and could mis-model the active-period chain or over-engineer for a drought that runs longer than the eclipse-T-45 / PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 signals suggest). I rank C #1 because its MAGNITUDE is highest and it is the bullseye on the operator's explicit criterion, but I am flagging honestly that its variance is also highest. A defensible alternative ordering is B > C > A. Operator's call on risk appetite.

A_prop_graph_archaeology.single_run_doable: Mostly. 127 PROPs is a large but mechanically-walkable corpus; the judgment layer narrows to ~10-20 cleanup candidates, which is one-run feasible.
A_prop_graph_archaeology.reasoning: PROP-102 (prop auto-close) and PROP-108 (directive auto-close) are both in shadow mode TODAY and will eventually go to enforce. Auto-close trusts the PROP dependency/status graph (supersedes_props, superseded_by_props, verification_pattern grade). A polluted graph -> wrong autonomous closures during the active period when nobody is watching closely. This run's PROP-102 walk already shows 38 grade_A / 48 grade_C / 38 field_gated across 127 PROPs and only 2 eligible-for-autoclose with 0 actually closing — a sign the trust graph is conservative but unaudited. Cleaning OBE-but-not-marked PROPs, fixing wrongly-graded verification_patterns, and repairing broken supersedes links NOW (a) de-risks enforce-mode flip and (b) trims the per-run walk that every tinker, prop-auto-close, and directive-auto-close pass pays. Time-sensitivity is the differentiator: this is cheapest to do before enforce, not after.
A_prop_graph_archaeology.deliverable: A one-time PROP-graph audit report (dependency graph + ~10-20 ranked cleanup candidates with proposed status flips), propose-only; operator/decider applies the flips.

B_prompt_cost_archaeology.single_run_doable: Yes. PROP-112 step-cost-history has ~13 decider rows + ~7 integrity rows on git HEAD — small but sufficient to rank the top-3 step buckets per agent and inspect the firing prompt sections.
B_prompt_cost_archaeology.reasoning: Decider is the busiest active-period agent (WIN intake, patches, commits, expansion integration); integrity runs daily regardless. A per-step cost slim (PROP-111 1B-style rare-path move to a reference module) compounds across every active-period run, so the saving GROWS exactly when cost pressure returns — the textbook 'save cost after dome returns' shape. Highest-confidence candidate because it is grounded in measured data, not simulation. Sample size is the only caveat (13 rows); top-bucket identification is robust to that, concrete diff sizing slightly less so.
B_prompt_cost_archaeology.deliverable: Top-3 cost step buckets per agent (decider + integrity) with concrete propose-only slim diffs for the top 1-2, mirroring PROP-111 1A/1C structure.

C_pre_active_period_readiness_audit.single_run_doable: Yes for the simulation + 1-2 proposals; the chain is well-understood from the prompts.
C_pre_active_period_readiness_audit.forward_value: VERY HIGH (magnitude); HIGH with execution-risk discount applied
C_pre_active_period_readiness_audit.reasoning: This is the ONLY candidate that proactively targets the specific active-period failure modes the operator is worried about: HOL blocking in analyst->curmudgeon->decider under a burst (e.g. 3 new WINs/day), cost spikes, and integrity-finding cascades on fresh/broken assertions. Eclipse T-45 and PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 closing in 2 days make the active-period transition genuinely near, so pre-emptive weak-link proposals have a real near-term payoff window. Execution-risk discount: output is a mental simulation, so it can mis-model the chain or over-engineer for hypotheticals; quality depends on naming SPECIFIC weak links with evidence from the current prompts, not generic 'add more capacity' hand-waving.
C_pre_active_period_readiness_audit.deliverable: A simulated-burst readiness report naming specific weak links with evidence, + 1-2 propose-only proposals for the highest-risk ones (acceptance criteria required).

D_disaster_recovery_playbook_expansion.probability_useful: low-moderate (disasters are rare) x very high magnitude when they hit
D_disaster_recovery_playbook_expansion.reasoning: PROP-051 covers only the workspace-sync mass-delete shape. The two MOST-LIKELY uncovered shapes are (a) chronic decider 403 cascade (the 'Devilwench' identity 403 has already happened repeatedly and has a proven Git-Data-API escape hatch worth codifying into a detect->diagnose->recover->verify playbook) and (b) PAT revoked mid-pipeline (single-point-of-failure; the recovery path — regenerate dome-scoped PAT, update workspace .git/config + both scheduled-task prompts — is tribal knowledge in CLAUDE.md, not a playbook). Forward-value is insurance: high payoff IF needed, but probabilistic. Strong #4, below the top 3 because the top 3 pay off in the EXPECTED active period, not only in the tail.
D_disaster_recovery_playbook_expansion.deliverable: Two propose-only playbooks (403-cascade + PAT-revoked) with detect/diagnose/recover/verify steps.

E_documentation_hygiene_pass.single_run_doable: Yes but breadth-risk: easily sprawls into a low-signal list.
E_documentation_hygiene_pass.reasoning: Tinker already runs a 'CLAUDE.md Accuracy & Performance Audit' every Mode 3 run, so the highest-value doc-drift checks happen routinely. A standalone deep-dive would mostly surface incremental staleness. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT commission as a standalone deep-dive; instead fold the high-signal doc-drift findings that Candidates A and C naturally surface (stale PROP refs, outdated cadence numbers near the agents they touch) into those deliverables.

F_cost_projection_model.reasoning: A forward burn model under activity intensity X is useful capacity planning, but its main consumer is the PROP-115 Recommendation B (Haiku gate) decision — which the operator has explicitly DEFERRED. Much of the needed data already exists in PROP-101 cost-history. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT commission standalone; fold a lightweight burn-projection appendix into Candidate B (which is already in the cost-data) so the operator gets the projection without a separate Opus run.

G_hnote_consumption_audit.reasoning: Tracing historical HNOTEs through their consuming agents is a genuinely tinker-unique cross-agent integrity check, and miscompiled HNOTEs have bitten before (the PROP-053 closure HNOTE lost for 23h). But the risk it targets is now partially mitigated by action-typed HNOTE handlers (PROP-058/PROP-098), and HNOTE volume is low. RECOMMENDATION: worthwhile but below the top 3; commission only after the top 3 are harvested, or run as a light add-on. Not a standalone priority deep-dive.

H_archive_integrity_audit.reasoning: The PROP-022 / PROP-065 archive files are critical infra, but they are already guarded by git-append-only discipline (PROP-065) plus the workspace-sync divergence canary that fires on any FUSE-newer divergence. No canary has fired. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT commission unless a divergence canary or the PROP-099 prune-resurrection canary actually trips (this run: prune-resurrection canary clean). Reactive, not proactive, value.

I_tinker_self_audit.forward_value: LOW-MODERATE; partially in tension with the reframe
I_tinker_self_audit.reasoning: tinker.md grew +15.4% since 2026-06-10 (PROP-102 + PROP-108 prose), and as the #1 cost agent, slimming rarely-fired sections has real direct cost value. BUT the operator just REJECTED the throttle direction and explicitly wants tinker MORE valuable during the quiet window, so a self-slim deep-dive partly relitigates the cost-cutting framing the operator set aside. The rarely-fired-section trim is pure efficiency (no capability loss) and worth doing eventually, but it is the LOWEST forward-value item here and slightly off-spirit. RECOMMENDATION: defer; revisit alongside PROP-115 Recommendation B (the deferred Haiku-gate engineering project), where prompt-structure work naturally belongs.

ranked_top_3.value_criterion_applied: Highest MAGNITUDE on the operator's explicit goal (smoother active-period transition); directly pre-empts HOL-blocking / cost-spike / integrity-cascade failure modes before eclipse-T-45 and PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 (closing in ~2d) plausibly re-activate the chain.
ranked_top_3.execution_risk: Highest of the top 3 — output is a simulation; must name SPECIFIC weak links with prompt-level evidence, not generic capacity advice.
ranked_top_3.scope_statement_for_operator: Commission tinker to run a single-pass pre-active-period readiness audit of the analyst -> curmudgeon -> decider chain under a simulated drought-break burst (assume 3 new dome WINs landing in one day plus the normal predictions/integrity follow-on). Walk each agent's prompt and cadence, identify where head-of-line blocking, cost spikes, or cascading integrity findings would emerge first, and rank the weak links by (likelihood-under-burst x recovery-cost). Deliverable: a readiness report naming each weak link with prompt/cadence evidence, plus propose-only PROP(s) for the 1-2 highest-risk links (each with explicit acceptance criteria). Out of scope: applying any fix, and any dome-tinker cadence change (throttle is rejected). Gate the run on producing the named-weak-link list — if no concrete weak link with evidence is found, report that and stop rather than manufacturing proposals.
